class="RichText__Container-sc-39eba4fb-0 bVHCgY"><p>Released in 1961, this song was <a href="https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2015/05/ben-e-king-dead-at-76-stand-by-me/392126/" rel="noopener nofollow">inspired by the spiritual hymn  “Lord Stand By Me”</a>. It has since been recorded into more than 400 other versions.</p>

<p>It was ranked the 122nd out of <em>Rolling Stones</em> <a href="https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/500-greatest-songs-of-all-time-151127/ben-e-king-stand-by-me-169932/" rel="noopener nofollow">“500 Greatest Songs of All Time”</a>. In 2012 it ranked as one of <a href="https://www.bmi.com/news/entry/stand_by_me_to_receive_towering_song_award_at_2012_songwriters_hall_of_fame" rel="noopener nofollow">BMI’s top 5 most performed songs</a> of the 20th century, with more than 11.6 million performances.</p>

<p>When it debuted in 1961, it <a href="https://www.billboard.com/music/ben-e-king/chart-history/BSI" rel="noopener nofollow">reached the Billboards #1 position</a> in “Hot R&B Singles.”</p>

King first offered it to his group, The Drifters but was told – <em>“Not a bad song, but we don’t need it.”</em></p>

<p>Once solo – He and Jerry Lieber went to work –</p>

<blockquote><p><em>I showed him the song. Did it on piano a little bit, he called the musicians back into the studio, and we went ahead and recorded it.</em></p></blockquote>

<p>And the rest is history.</p>
